cwe.name: SQL Injection
cwe.description: Untrusted input is concatenated into SQL queries, allowing attackers to modify query semantics, bypass authentication, exfiltrate data, or execute database commands.

cwe.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
cwe.description: Untrusted data is rendered into HTML/JavaScript/URL/CSS context without proper escaping, enabling script execution in victim browsers.

cwe.name: OS Command Injection
cwe.description: Untrusted input is used to construct operating system commands executed via Runtime.exec, ProcessBuilder, system(), popen(), or exec().

cwe.name: Code Injection
cwe.description: Untrusted input is evaluated as code by the application via eval(), expression languages, template engines, script engines, ClassLoader, or reflection.

cwe.name: Expression Language Injection (SSTI)
cwe.description: Untrusted input is injected into an expression language (SpEL, OGNL, MVEL, JEXL) or template engine (Freemarker, Velocity, Thymeleaf, Jinja2, Jade/Pug), enabling remote code execution or data exfiltration.

cwe.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
cwe.description: Application deserializes data from untrusted sources using ObjectInputStream, Jackson polymorphic typing, SnakeYAML, XStream, Kryo, FST, Hessian, or native pickle/unmarshal, enabling arbitrary code execution via gadget chains.

cwe.name: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
cwe.description: XML parser is configured to process external entities, enabling file disclosure, SSRF, denial of service (Billion Laughs), and in some cases remote code execution.

cwe.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
cwe.description: Server fetches URLs controlled by attacker, enabling access to internal networks, cloud metadata endpoints, and internal services.

cwe.name: Path Traversal
cwe.description: User input is used to construct file paths without validation or canonicalization, enabling access outside intended directory (including Zip/Tar slip).

cwe.name: Unrestricted File Upload
cwe.description: Application accepts file uploads without proper validation of type, content, size, or name, enabling malicious file execution, path traversal, or DoS.

cwe.name: Out-of-Bounds Write
cwe.description: Software writes data past the end or before the beginning of an allocated buffer, enabling memory corruption (heap/stack overflow).

cwe.name: Out-of-Bounds Read
cwe.description: Software reads data past the end or before the beginning of an allocated buffer, enabling information disclosure (Heartbleed-class).

cwe.name: Use After Free
cwe.description: Memory is referenced after it has been freed, enabling arbitrary code execution via heap manipulation and dangling pointer exploitation.

cwe.name: Integer Overflow
cwe.description: Arithmetic operation produces a value outside the representable range, leading to buffer allocation errors, negative size bugs, and memory corruption.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Commands
cwe.description: Application constructs command strings using external input without proper neutralization of special characters ($, ;, |, &&, ||, etc.).

cwe.name: LDAP Injection
cwe.description: Untrusted input is incorporated into LDAP search filters without proper escaping, enabling query manipulation, authentication bypass, and information disclosure.

cwe.name: XPath Injection
cwe.description: Untrusted input is used to construct XPath queries, enabling query manipulation, authentication bypass, and data extraction from XML documents.

cwe.name: CRLF Injection (HTTP Response Splitting)
cwe.description: Untrusted input containing carriage return and line feed characters is written to HTTP response headers, enabling header injection, cache poisoning, and XSS.

cwe.name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)
cwe.description: Application performs HTTP redirect to a URL from user input without validation, enabling phishing and OAuth token theft.

cwe.name: Insecure Cookie Configuration (Missing Secure Flag)
cwe.description: Cookies containing session tokens lack the Secure or HttpOnly flags, enabling theft via MITM or client-side script access.

cwe.name: Unsafe Reflection
cwe.description: Application uses reflection to access classes, methods, or fields using untrusted names, enabling code execution or information disclosure.

cwe.name: Authentication Bypass
cwe.description: Authentication mechanism can be bypassed via parameter tampering, missing checks, race conditions, or path traversal in auth flow.

cwe.name: Missing Authorization
cwe.description: Application does not verify that the authenticated user is authorized to access a resource or perform an action (missing access control check).

cwe.name: Incorrect Authorization
cwe.description: Authorization check is present but incorrectly implemented, allowing privilege escalation or horizontal access to other users' resources.

cwe.name: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR)
cwe.description: Application exposes direct references (IDs, keys) to internal objects without verifying the user's ownership or access rights.

cwe.name: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwe.description: Sensitive endpoints or administrative functions lack any authentication requirement, exposing them to anonymous access.

cwe.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
cwe.description: Application does not verify that state-changing requests were intentionally sent by the authenticated user, enabling forced actions.

cwe.name: Hardcoded Credentials
cwe.description: Credentials, API keys, tokens, or cryptographic material are hardcoded in source code, configuration files, or build artifacts.

cwe.name: Improper Privilege Management
cwe.description: Application fails to properly isolate privilege levels, enabling lower-privileged code to perform higher-privileged operations.

cwe.name: Use of Weak Cryptographic Algorithm
cwe.description: Application uses broken or weak cryptographic algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, DES, RC4, ECB mode, static IV, predictable seeds).

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation
cwe.description: TLS/SSL certificates are not properly validated (trust-all managers, hostname verifiers that accept all), enabling man-in-the-middle attacks.

cwe.name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
cwe.description: Cryptographic algorithm is configured with insufficient key size (RSA < 2048 bits, AES 128 in high-security contexts).

cwe.name: Use of Weak Hash
cwe.description: Application uses weak hashing algorithms (MD4, MD5, SHA-1) for security-sensitive purposes such as password storage or digital signatures.

cwe.name: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
cwe.description: Sensitive data (credentials, tokens, PII) is transmitted over unencrypted channels (HTTP, plain JDBC, unencrypted messaging).

cwe.name: Race Condition (TOCTOU)
cwe.description: Concurrent operations on shared resources without proper synchronization, enabling time-of-check-time-of-use (TOCTOU) attacks on file and database operations.

cwe.name: Resource Exhaustion
cwe.description: Application does not limit resource consumption (memory, CPU, file descriptors, threads), enabling denial of service via ReDoS, Billion Laughs, or CPU exhaustion.

cwe.name: Uncontrolled Memory Allocation
cwe.description: Allocation size is controlled by user input without limits or validation, enabling memory exhaustion, Zip Bomb, or heap overflow.

cwe.name: Information Disclosure
cwe.description: Application exposes sensitive information such as stack traces, error messages, debug output, version banners, or internal paths.

cwe.name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
cwe.description: Error messages returned to users contain database schemas, file paths, stack traces, or other internal implementation details.

cwe.name: Incorrect Default Permissions
cwe.description: Files, directories, or IPC resources are created with overly permissive defaults (world-readable, world-writable), enabling unauthorized access.

cwe.name: Exposed Dangerous Method or Function
cwe.description: Application exposes dangerous functions (exit, stop, exec, defineClass, newProxyInstance) to untrusted callers.

cwe.name: Improper Input Validation
cwe.description: Input is not validated for type, range, format, length, or semantics before processing, enabling a wide range of injection and corruption attacks.

cwe.name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
cwe.description: Output is not properly encoded or escaped for its target context (HTML, URL, JS, SQL, LDAP, XML), enabling injection across boundaries.

cwe.name: Business Logic Error
cwe.description: Application logic does not properly enforce business rules (negative quantities, skipping checkout steps, bypassing verification), enabling fraud and abuse.

cwe.name: Prototype Pollution
cwe.description: Merging or cloning controlled by user input modifies the prototype of objects, injecting properties into all instances and enabling property injection, privilege escalation, or XSS in Node.js/JavaScript.

cwe.name: Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
cwe.description: Regular expression with exponential backtracking can be exploited with crafted input to consume CPU for excessive time.

cwe.name: CSV Injection (Formula Injection)
cwe.description: CSV exports contain user-controlled data starting with =, @, +, or -, enabling formula execution when opened in Excel/Google Sheets.

cwe.name: Format String Vulnerability
cwe.description: User-controlled format string is passed to printf/sprintf/fprintf family functions, enabling arbitrary memory read/write.

cwe.name: NULL Pointer Dereference
cwe.description: Application dereferences a NULL pointer, causing denial of service (crash/segfault) or potentially exploitable conditions.

cwe.name: Improper Check for Exceptional Conditions
cwe.description: Application does not properly handle or check for exceptional conditions, leading to unexpected behavior and potential security bypass.

cwe.name: Insecure Temporary File
cwe.description: Temporary files are created insecurely (predictable names, shared directories, no exclusive creation), enabling privilege escalation or symlink attacks.

cwe.name: Unchecked Return Value
cwe.description: Return value of security-critical function (e.g., wait, flush, allocate, setuid) is ignored, leading to unpredictable state.

cwe.name: Infinite Loop
cwe.description: Loop termination condition depends on untrusted input without proper bounds, enabling denial of service via infinite execution.

cwe.name: Heap-based Buffer Overflow
cwe.description: Heap allocation boundaries are exceeded, overwriting adjacent heap metadata or data structures, enabling arbitrary code execution.

cwe.name: Stack-based Buffer Overflow
cwe.description: Stack buffer boundaries are exceeded (via strcpy, gets, sprintf without bounds), overwriting return addresses and enabling RCE.

cwe.name: Integer Underflow
cwe.description: Arithmetic subtraction or decrement wraps below the minimum representable value, leading to unexpected large values and memory corruption.

cwe.name: Missing Release of Memory (Memory Leak)
cwe.description: Dynamically allocated memory is never freed, leaking resources and potentially enabling denial of service.

cwe.name: Double Free
cwe.description: Same memory address is freed twice, corrupting heap management data structures and enabling arbitrary code execution.

cwe.name: Type Confusion
cwe.description: Object is accessed as if it were a different type, bypassing vtable dispatch safety and enabling code execution (C++ dynamic_cast bypass, Java type confusion in deserialization).

cwe.name: Missing Release of Resource (File Descriptors, Connections)
cwe.description: System resources (file descriptors, database connections, sockets) are never released, enabling resource exhaustion DoS.

cwe.name: Incorrect Calculation of Buffer Size
cwe.description: Buffer size is incorrectly calculated (off-by-one, sizeof vs strlen confusion, forgetting null terminator), leading to overflow.

cwe.name: Origin Validation Error
cwe.description: Application does not validate the origin of network messages, enabling cross-origin attacks in WebSocket and postMessage contexts.

cwe.name: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
cwe.description: Application fails to verify cryptographic signatures on data or messages, enabling forgery and tampering.

cwe.name: Weak Password Requirements
cwe.description: Password policy allows weak passwords (short length, no complexity, common passwords), enabling brute force attacks.

cwe.name: Insufficient Session Expiration
cwe.description: Session tokens do not expire after logout or remain valid indefinitely, enabling session hijacking via stolen tokens.

cwe.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment
cwe.description: Critical resources (config files, databases, sockets) have incorrect permission assignments allowing unauthorized access.

cwe.name: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
cwe.description: Application uses predictable random number generators (java.util.Random, Math.random, rand()) for security-sensitive purposes such as token generation.

cwe.name: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwe.description: Credentials are stored or transmitted without adequate protection (plaintext storage, stored in cookies, logged to disk).

cwe.name: Use of Cryptographically Weak PRNG
cwe.description: Pseudorandom number generator is seeded with predictable values (time, PID, static seed), enabling prediction of tokens and keys.

cwe.name: Improper Restriction of Operations within Bounds of Memory Buffer
cwe.description: Generic buffer overflow covering stack, heap, and BSS/data segment overflows due to missing or incorrect bounds checking.

cwe.name: Improper Validation of Array Index
cwe.description: Array index is derived from untrusted input without bounds checking, enabling out-of-bounds read/write.

cwe.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log Files
cwe.description: Sensitive data (credentials, PII, tokens) is written to log files, enabling leakage via log aggregation or unauthorized log access.

cwe.name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
cwe.description: Sensitive data is stored in unencrypted form in databases, files, or SharedPreferences/UserDefaults.

cwe.name: Exposure of System Data to Unauthorized Control Sphere
cwe.description: Internal system data (environment variables, configuration, debug endpoints) is exposed to unauthorized control sphere.

cwe.name: Use of Obsolete Function
cwe.description: Application uses deprecated, insecure API functions (gets, strcpy, Thread.stop, XMLDecoder), retaining known vulnerabilities.

cwe.name: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
cwe.description: Application uses functions known to be dangerous when used improperly (memcpy, strcat, sprintf vs snprintf).

cwe.name: Use of Uninitialized Variable
cwe.description: Variable is used before being initialized, leading to undefined behavior and potential information disclosure.

cwe.name: Improper Initialization
cwe.description: Security-relevant resources or data structures are improperly initialized, leaving them in insecure default state.

cwe.name: Improper Handling of Unexpected Data Type
cwe.description: Application does not handle unexpected input types, leading to type confusion, conversion errors, or crashes.

cwe.name: Reachable Assertion
cwe.description: Assert statements that can be triggered by external input are reachable, leading to DoS when assertions are enabled.

cwe.name: Session Fixation
cwe.description: Application allows an attacker to fixate a user's session identifier before authentication, enabling hijacking after login.

cwe.name: Use of Wrong Operator in String Comparison
cwe.description: Identity operator (==, is) used instead of equality operator (.equals(), == in Python) for string comparison, enabling authentication bypass.

cwe.name: Use of Unmaintained Third-Party Components
cwe.description: Application depends on libraries or frameworks that are no longer maintained, accumulating unpatched known vulnerabilities.

cwe.name: CSV Injection
cwe.description: CSV export cells start with dangerous characters (=, +, -, @) that Excel interprets as formulas, enabling code execution.

cwe.name: Insufficient Logging
cwe.description: Security-relevant events (authentication attempts, authorization failures, input validation errors) are not adequately logged.
